intent: 24 dishes that are genuinely five ingredient lines or fewer — counting every line, including salt and oil. The catalogue has FOUR of those against a target of about 44, and a short list is the strongest predictor of a recipe a real Egyptian kitchen can actually reach: the dataset audit finds 0 or 1 exact matches for a three-item pantry today. No recipe is written yet. These are dish identities, sent to the photography preflight first, so that the recipes get written for the dishes that can honestly be illustrated rather than the other way round.

candidates.name: Hibiscus Tea
candidates.note: Three ingredients, drunk hot in winter and iced all summer, and in almost every Egyptian house during Ramadan. Nothing in the catalogue covers it.

candidates.name: Warm Sahlab with Pistachios
candidates.note: The winter drink. The sahlab row was added in Stage 2D and no recipe uses it.

candidates.name: Apricot Nectar
candidates.note: The Ramadan drink, from the apricot sheet sold by the kilo. The ingredient row is literally named qamar el din and nothing cooks with it.

candidates.name: Wheat Berries in Sweet Milk
candidates.note: Breakfast and a Mawlid sweet. Four lines, one pot, and the cheapest hot breakfast in the catalogue if it lands. No image at all on the first pass; this is the one alternative-name attempt before it is deferred. `ashure` is the Turkish dish of the same wheat, which Commons does have a category for.

candidates.name: Grilled Corn on the Cob
candidates.note: Street food on every corniche in the country, and four ingredients.

candidates.name: Roasted Sweet Potato
candidates.note: The winter counterpart to the corn cart. Cheap, filling, and nothing in the catalogue uses sweet potato except air-fryer fries.

candidates.name: Tahini Sauce with Lemon
candidates.note: Poured over taameya, fish, koshari and half the rest of the catalogue. It exists as an assumed accompaniment everywhere and as a recipe nowhere.

candidates.name: Honey-Soaked Dough Balls
candidates.note: Ramadan dessert made from flour and nothing else expensive. Five lines exactly.

candidates.name: Peanut and Sesame Dukkah
candidates.note: Bread dipped in oil then in this. The dukkah row exists as a bought blend; making it is five pantry items and a pan.

candidates.name: Fresh Lemonade with Mint
candidates.note: Four ingredients, and the thing an Egyptian kitchen makes when it has lemons and nothing else.

candidates.name: Tomato Soup
candidates.note: The soup made from whatever tomatoes are going soft. Five lines, no stock, no cream.

candidates.name: Eggs with Basterma
candidates.note: The Egyptian breakfast that is worth getting up for, and the only savoury protein dish in this batch. Four lines.

candidates.name: Pink Pickled Turnips
candidates.note: On the table beside foul and koshari everywhere. Five ingredients and a jar; the beetroot is only there for the colour.

candidates.name: Grilled Halloumi with Lemon
candidates.note: Four ingredients and eight minutes. The halloumi row is used by nothing.

candidates.name: Parmesan and Black Pepper Pasta
candidates.note: Renamed in Stage 3P.2. The photograph found under "cacio e pepe" is kept because a pecorino sauce and a Parmesan one are visually identical on pasta, but the recipe no longer claims to be the Roman dish: there is no pecorino row and one dish does not justify opening the ingredient ontology.

candidates.name: Olive Oil Flatbread
candidates.note: Five ingredients, none of them perishable, and a proof that the catalogue's bread section is not only Egyptian.

candidates.name: Garlic Butter Bread
candidates.note: Made here on baladi bread rather than a baguette, which is what an Egyptian kitchen actually has.

candidates.name: French Toast
candidates.note: Stale toast bread, five lines, and a breakfast a child can make. Breakfast is the thinnest meal type in the catalogue at 29 of 161.

candidates.name: Crisp Potato Hash Browns
candidates.note: Potatoes and onions, which is what is in the kitchen when nothing else is.

candidates.name: Buttery Mashed Potatoes
candidates.note: The side dish the catalogue has never had, at five lines.

candidates.name: Mango Yogurt Drink
candidates.note: Egypt grows more mangoes than it knows what to do with between June and September.

candidates.name: Spiced Milk Tea
candidates.note: Five pantry items. The tea row is used by nothing at all.

candidates.name: Turkish Coffee
candidates.note: Three ingredients and a kanaka. Drunk in Egypt at least as much as in Turkey; tagged Turkish because that is what the dish is called.

candidates.name: Mashed Spiced Beans
candidates.note: A tin of beans, an onion and a pan. Legumes are the catalogue's joint-largest protein group and this is the cheapest five-line member of it.
